note: Salesforce docs describe per-user OAuth 2.0 (with PKCE) via External Client Apps / Connected Apps as the authorization path for API and MCP clients.
API access is enabled by default in Developer Edition orgs, and Developer Edition is a free self-serve signup.
REST API is the primary documented integration surface; SOAP, GraphQL and Pub/Sub (gRPC) exist alongside it.
Salesforce Hosted MCP Servers are documented on developer.salesforce.com and hosted by Salesforce (forcedotcom/mcp-hosted repo says they are GA).
Buildable on a free Developer Edition, but customer orgs on Professional Edition need an API add-on and each org must enable/authorize the external client app, so caveats apply.
Multi-account (marketplace/private distribution) apps use OAuth; static-token apps are limited to one account.

Verifier agreed with self_serve_free, but researcher.md defines 'free sandbox, production needs review' as approval_required; HubSpot caps unlisted OAuth apps at 25 installs until review. Researcher and verifier were both wrong by the spec.
API reference shows resource-oriented HTTP endpoints such as GET /crm/objects/.../contacts on api.hubapi.com.
HubSpot documents a publicly hosted remote MCP server at https://mcp.hubspot.com using OAuth.
Self-serve build/test works, but unlisted marketplace OAuth apps are capped at 25 installs until reviewed and listed, and some APIs need paid hubs.
Verifier was right; confirmed on the page.
Cloud has no free plan (30-day no-card trial), but 'Self-hosting the open source core is free', giving $0 working credentials; borderline with self_serve_trial if only Cloud is considered.
Docs state the Core and Metadata APIs are both available as REST and GraphQL. (API offered in both styles; either accepted)
Docs say 'Twenty exposes an MCP server' at https://{workspace}/mcp for Cloud and self-hosted, with OAuth or API key.
Self-serve Cloud trial and free self-hosting allow building and testing today with no review gate.
API v2 authentication section: use your personal API key via HTTP Basic (apikey:X); no OAuth flow is documented.
Pricing lists only paid plans (Growth/Pro/Enterprise) plus a 14-day trial of the Enterprise plan; no free plan.
Freshdesk API v2 is a REST/JSON API.
Freshworks documents its own MCP server at https://<subdomain>.freshdesk.com/mcp (API-key auth), GA from September 10, 2026, on Growth/Pro/Enterprise.
Buildable via a self-serve trial, but continued testing requires a paid plan after 14 days.
'OAuth is required for public integrations available to all Front customers unless you obtain an exception from us.'
A free development account is self-serve, but apps are private to their instance until published, and publishing requires Front to test and technically approve the integration.
Front's Core API is a REST API accessed with OAuth or API tokens.
Front documents its own MCP server at https://mcp.frontapp.com/mcp with OAuth via app.frontapp.com.
Buildable on a free dev account, but multi-customer distribution needs publishing/approval and OAuth must be authorized by company admins.
'Gladly API uses token-based Basic Authentication' with agent email as username and API token as password.
Tokens are created inside a customer's Gladly org by users granted the API User role by a Gladly admin; gladly.com offers only 'Get a demo'/contact sales, no self-serve signup.
Gladly publishes a REST API reference.

Gladly's help center (published 2026-11-18) documents the 'Gladly MCP for Claude' connector plus plugin at github.com/gladly/claude-plugin; scoped to Gladly AI (Guides, Workflows, sessions) and must be enabled per org by Gladly.
API is usable once inside a customer org (sandbox env at {org}.gladly.qa exists), so the enterprise-customer gate limits testing rather than fully blocking it.
Requests use HTTP Basic with API key SID/secret (default) or Account SID/Auth Token.
'Trial accounts expire 30 days after sign-up'; afterwards you must upgrade to keep building.
'Twilio APIs use standard RESTful HTTP methods to perform actions on resources.'
Twilio hosts a docs MCP at mcp.twilio.com/docs (Public Beta, no account actions), and its twilio-labs GitHub org publishes @twilio-alpha/mcp exposing Twilio APIs.
Self-serve trial credentials allow building and testing immediately; trial limits (30 days, verified recipients) are not an approval gate.
OAuth is the method for apps serving multiple Aircall customers; Basic api_id:api_token is for a company's own account.
OAuth credentials come from the Tech Partner program ('apply to the Tech Partner program'); only own-account Basic keys are available via a customer/trial account.
Aircall Public API is a REST API at api.aircall.io/v1.
Aircall's MCP FAQ says it does not offer an MCP server yet; existing Aircall MCP servers are third-party (e.g. themobilefirstco, StackOne).
API access is on all plans and a free test period exists for Basic-key testing, but OAuth distribution requires Tech Partner status.
API key/secret (Basic) is accepted by 19 of 25 listed APIs (Accounts, Numbers, SMS, Messages, Verify2...); Vonage recommends JWT for most use-cases and Voice/Video require JWT.
Signup gives €2 free credit with test-number restrictions and no stated time limit, so credentials are obtainable at $0.
Vonage APIs are HTTP REST APIs authenticated via Authorization header.
Vonage publishes a hosted Documentation MCP and the @vonage/vonage-mcp-server-api-bindings tooling server (balance, sms, numbers), documented on developer.vonage.com.
Self-serve free credit lets a toolkit be built and tested today; demo-mode limits only restrict destinations.
Confirmed developer tokens sunset 2026-09-09; access is per Cloud project, OAuth.
Enabling the API grants only Test access; production needs an Explorer application (automated review in most cases), and Basic/Standard need brand verification or manual audit.
'The Google Ads API can be called either using gRPC or REST'; official client libraries are gRPC-based. (API offered in both styles; either accepted)
Google's own googleads GitHub org publishes google-ads-mcp and Google's developer docs provide its integration guide.
Buildable against test accounts immediately, but production access requires an access-level application/review.
API reference says to attach the public API key to the X-API-Key header of each request; it is the only method offered.
systeme.io has a never-expiring Free plan (pricing FAQ) and its MCP page says the MCP/API-key feature is included in all plans including Free; API reference states no plan restriction.
Docs say the public API follows RESTful conventions.
systeme.io's own developer docs document the Systeme.io MCP server (MCP key via X-MCP-Key header); the snzeeee GitHub server is a separate community project.
Self-serve API key from account settings on a free account with documented REST endpoints means a toolkit can be built and tested today.
v3 API is authenticated with an API key sent as 'Authorization: Bearer <API key>'; no OAuth is documented.
New accounts since March 25, 2025 get a 60-day free trial (100 emails/day); after it ends API-key integrations stop sending unless a paid plan is chosen; the free plan was retired.
SendGrid Web API v3 is an HTTP/JSON REST API (SMTP relay is secondary).

Twilio's only hosted MCP (mcp.twilio.com/docs) is documentation search that indexes SendGrid docs but 'does not connect to a Twilio account or execute any API calls'; execute-capable tools are listed as future, and twilio-labs/mcp exposes Twilio's Public API, not SendGrid v3 — so API-capable SendGrid MCPs are community only.
API keys can be created during the self-serve trial, but sending stops after 60 days without a paid plan, which is a caveat on testing/launch.
Apps created in the Dev Dashboard (public and custom) obtain access tokens through OAuth, sent as X-Shopify-Access-Token.
Development stores and custom apps need no approval, but distributing to many merchants requires public distribution, which the page lists as 'Approval required: Yes' (App Store review).
REST Admin API is legacy since Oct 1, 2024 and new public apps must use the GraphQL Admin API from April 1, 2025, so GraphQL is primary as claimed. (API offered in both styles; either accepted)
Shopify documents its own Dev MCP server (@shopify/dev-mcp) and store-hosted UCP/Checkout/Customer Accounts MCP servers on shopify.dev.
Buildable and testable on free development stores, but multi-merchant launch requires public-distribution approval.
Over HTTPS the REST API uses HTTP Basic Auth with the consumer key as username and consumer secret as password (OAuth 1.0a one-legged only over plain HTTP).
Keys are self-generated at WooCommerce > Settings > Advanced > REST API (or via the /wc-auth/v1/authorize endpoint) on the free open-source plugin; no vendor gate.
WooCommerce exposes a REST API under /wp-json/wc/v3.
WooCommerce's developer docs document its MCP integration (developer preview): WooCommerce abilities served via the WordPress MCP Adapter and Automattic's @automattic/mcp-wordpress-remote proxy.
Buildable today, but each store is self-hosted so base URL and keys are per-tenant, and the MCP is a developer preview subject to breaking changes.
SCAPI/OCAPI calls use an Account Manager API client via OAuth (sign-in, client credentials or JWT); Shopper APIs use SLAS OAuth.
Sandboxes require the organization to purchase sandbox credits and a realm ID obtained from the account executive, plus Account Manager roles — no self-serve developer path.
Salesforce Commerce API (SCAPI) and OCAPI are HTTP/JSON REST APIs authenticated with OAuth bearer tokens.
The B2C DX MCP server (@salesforce/b2c-dx-mcp) is published by Salesforce (SalesforceCommerceCloud org, Salesforce copyright) and can run Commerce API operations.
Gate is being an enterprise customer/partner with a realm, which the verdict enum lists under ready_with_caveats; borderline with blocked since no self-serve sandbox exists for a toolkit builder.
HTTP Basic authentication with API login and auto-generated API password is the only way to access the API.
Sandbox is 'completely free for any registered user' (dummy data, not billed); real data is pay-as-you-go — fits the free-sandbox definition.
DataForSEO v3 is an HTTP/JSON REST API.
DataForSEO's own page links github.com/dataforseo/mcp-server-typescript, npm dataforseo-mcp-server, Docker dataforseo/mcp, and a hosted endpoint mcp.dataforseo.com.
Self-serve credentials plus a free sandbox allow building and testing today.
All API endpoints require an API token passed in the x-api-token header.
Billing docs list a 'Scraper Free' plan with API tokens and say it includes 100 tokens per month with no credit card required.
API overview says it is built on REST principles with JSON bodies.
Docs call it 'the official Model Context Protocol server for MrScraper' (@mrscraper/mcp), hosted at mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp with OAuth 2.1 or API-key fallback.
Free plan with API tokens means a toolkit can be built and tested today with self-serve credentials.
Docs say to send your API key in the x-api-key header to https://api.waterfall.io.
API access is not self-serve: a team member reviews each key request (work email or booked call) and pricing is discussed on the call — a contact-sales gate.
HTTP JSON launcher/finder endpoints under api.waterfall.io with an OpenAPI spec.

Waterfall's agent docs offer only two agent skills (waterfall-direct-api, waterfall-integration) and the docs index has no MCP page; search found only unrelated 'waterfall enrichment' MCPs (Workato, LeadEnrich).
Usable documented API, but credentials require a sales-reviewed request, limiting testing until approved.
Since June 2026 developers can create self-managed OAuth clients (Authorization Code + PKCE) and make them public after domain verification; API tokens remain the alternative for direct API use.
OAuth is available on all plans including Free, and API tokens can be created on any free account.
Cloudflare API v4 is REST (a GraphQL Analytics API exists but is secondary).
Cloudflare hosts managed remote MCP servers, including the Cloudflare API MCP server at mcp.cloudflare.com/mcp covering 2,500+ endpoints with OAuth.
Free self-serve credentials, OAuth for third parties and a broad REST API allow building and testing today.
SQL API supports OAuth and key-pair JWT (plus programmatic access tokens); Snowflake's MCP docs recommend OAuth, with PAT only as fallback.
Trial runs 30 days or until the free usage balance is depleted, then the account is suspended until a credit card is added and it is upgraded; no permanent free plan.
Snowflake SQL API and Snowflake REST APIs are HTTP REST endpoints (drivers are the other access path).
Snowflake-managed MCP server (GA Nov 2025) is hosted by Snowflake and exposes Cortex Analyst/Search/Agents and SQL execution tools.
Buildable via self-serve 30-day trial, but continued testing needs a paid account and OAuth requires per-account security-integration setup.
Datadog API auth page: write requests require an API key and read requests also require an application key; no OAuth described for general API use.
Pricing page offers a permanent Free tier ('up to five Basic hosts with 1-day metric retention, at no cost') and says trials can move to the Free tier, so credentials are obtainable at $0.
Datadog's API reference is an HTTP/JSON REST API authenticated with API/application keys.
Datadog's own docs describe the 'Remote Datadog MCP Server' that provides remote access to most Datadog products (noted as under significant development, not GovCloud).
Free tier plus self-serve API/app keys means a toolkit can be built and tested today without gates.
Atlassian docs describe OAuth 2.0 (3LO) apps created self-serve in the developer console; basic auth/API tokens are only for simple scripts and collecting customer tokens is discouraged.
Jira pricing lists a Free plan, and 3LO apps can be created and shared without mandatory review (unreviewed apps only show a warning).
Jira Cloud platform is accessed via REST APIs (page refers to making REST API calls with 3LO or basic auth).
Atlassian developer docs describe its cloud-hosted Rovo MCP server at https://mcp.atlassian.com/v2/mcp.
Free site plus self-serve OAuth 3LO app creation allows building and testing today; review only affects the 'unreviewed app' warning.
Asana auth docs say OAuth is 'the best choice if multiple users need to sign in to your app'; PATs are for scripts, service accounts are Enterprise-only.
Asana developer overview says you can 'create a free account' to build/test (sandbox only needed for premium features).
Quick start uses REST endpoints such as https://app.asana.com/api/1.0/workspaces with a PAT.
Asana's developer docs state 'Asana offers a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server' hosted at https://mcp.asana.com/v2/mcp.
Free account plus self-serve OAuth/PAT credentials; no review gate stated for building and testing.
Coda (now Superhuman Docs) API reference uses 'Authorization: Bearer <your API token>' user API tokens; no OAuth for third-party API apps is described.
API page: 'We make the Superhuman Docs API available to all of our users free of charge, in both free and paid workspaces.'
Coda API v1 is a REST/JSON API (GET/POST/PUT/PATCH endpoints with rate limits per method).

Coda's own guide says 'Superhuman Docs runs an MCP server built on the open Model Context Protocol standard' (endpoint coda.io/apis/mcp per its help center); community servers also exist but the vendor one is first-party.
Verifier was right; token-only auth is not a gate under the verdict definition.
Stripe docs: 'Stripe uses API keys to authenticate requests' (secret/restricted/agent keys); OAuth exists for Connect/Apps/MCP but API keys are the core API auth.
Any account gets sandbox test keys (sk_test_/rk_test_) for free to build and test; live keys come with account activation.
Stripe API is a REST API (v1 and v2 endpoints) authenticated by API keys.
Stripe docs document its own hosted MCP server at https://mcp.stripe.com with OAuth or agent API keys.
Free sandbox keys allow a toolkit to be built and tested today.
SIGNED endpoints need an API key plus a request signature; 'We support HMAC, RSA, and Ed25519 keys' (Ed25519 recommended, still a signature scheme).
Spot Test Network gives API keys free via 'Log In with GitHub' with virtual funds; live keys need 2FA, KYC and a deposit of any amount (FAQ 360002502072) but no approval.
Binance Spot API docs are organized as REST API (with WebSocket API/streams alongside); primary style REST matches.
Binance Developer Docs document 'a Binance AI Tool' MCP server at https://agent.binance.com/mcp/agentic (Agent OS); the many GitHub Binance MCPs are community.
Buildable on testnet today, but live keys require KYC, 2FA and a deposit (and regional restrictions), which limits launch.
Xero API access is OAuth2 (custom connections with client ID/secret or OAuth bearer tokens), as documented in Xero's own repo.
Xero developer pricing has a Starter tier at $0 with 5 connections and no certification required; higher tiers are paid and Plus+ need App Certification.
Xero's Accounting API and related APIs are REST/JSON APIs wrapped by the MCP server.
The MCP server is published in Xero's XeroAPI GitHub org as @xeroapi/xero-mcp-server (local npx server).
Testable free on Starter (5 connections) but scaling needs paid tiers and App Certification/security assessment.
Fathom supports API keys for personal use and OAuth apps for integrations other users install; OAuth app registration is a self-serve form (fathom.video/marketplace_applications/new).
Fathom API page: 'API keys, webhooks, and SDKs are included on every Fathom plan, including Free.'
API overview: 'All REST API resources are authenticated with API keys generated via the Fathom website's settings area.'
Fathom's developer docs describe an 'official MCP (Model Context Protocol) server' at https://api.fathom.ai/mcp.
Free plan includes API keys and OAuth apps are self-registered; review only applies to promotion.
Quickstart uses 'Authorization: Bearer $REDUCTO_API_KEY' with keys created in Studio.
Pricing: Standard plan includes '$150 in free usage' (no time limit stated) and quickstart says sign up for a free account and create a key.
Quickstart shows cURL REST calls (plus SDKs wrapping the REST API).
Reducto docs document a hosted MCP server at https://mcp.reducto.ai/mcp and local package mcp-server-reducto.
Free account with self-serve API key lets a toolkit be built and tested today.
Devin API uses service-user credentials / PATs (cog_ prefix) sent as Bearer tokens, i.e. API keys.
Pricing comparison table marks 'Devin API' as not included on Free ($0) and included on Pro ($20/mo), Max, Teams and Enterprise.
Devin API reference is a REST API (v3 organization/enterprise endpoints, legacy v1/v2).
Devin docs document the official Devin MCP server at https://mcp.devin.ai/mcp using a Devin API key.
Buildable with self-serve keys but requires at least the paid Pro plan, a paid-tier gate.
Apps must be registered for a Client ID/Client Secret and use OAuth2 server-side or client-side flows; username/password flow is described as a last resort.

The $0 Free plan lists 'API Integrations: 1000 calls per hour', and developers.podio.com/api-key says you just sign up and open the API key tab; no app review or install cap is documented (limits are per user per key, add-ons only raise rate).
Podio API is a JSON-over-HTTPS REST API called with an OAuth2 Authorization header.
Vendor (Progress) documentation says the Podio MCP Server is live at https://mcp.podio.com/mcp with OAuth; it is in beta.
Free self-serve keys with no review; only gate is rate limits (1,000 calls/hour per user per key), which does not block building or testing.
Clients are registered in the Zoho Developer Console to get Client ID/Secret; server-based apps are 'intended for use by multiple Zoho accounts'.
The credit table includes 'Free Edition | 5000 credits', so the API works on the free edition; client registration is self-serve with no review or install cap described.
Zoho CRM API v8 is a REST API metered by credits.
Zoho CRM developer docs: 'Zoho CRM provides these as pre-built MCP servers, so you don't need to build, host, or maintain any infrastructure.'
Self-serve OAuth client plus free-edition API credits allow building and testing today.
Admins generate API keys under Settings > Integrations > API Keys; OAuth client credentials are not self-serve, so a toolkit would use API keys.

OAuth apps can only be registered by contacting Copper ('To register your application, contact us' -> partners@copper.com), an approval gate for multi-tenant install; the Developer API is Professional/Business-tier only (support article 9623758) but every plan has a 14-day free trial, so per v2 precedence approval_required holds (would be paid_plan only if trials exclude the API, which docs do not say).
Copper Developer API is a REST/JSON API documented per resource (people, companies, opportunities, etc.).
Copper's page says an official MCP server is 'COMING SOON' with beta launching November 2026 but documents no endpoint; a marketing announcement alone counts as none_found.
'Developer API' is listed only for Professional (and Business) tiers and OAuth needs Copper registration, so buildable but gated.
Users enable and copy an API Key from their Profile; it is exchanged (with client ID) for a 15-minute token via OAuth2 client_credentials, so the end-user credential is an API key.

DealCloud offers only 'Schedule a demo' (no trial/self-serve signup); API capability must be enabled by a site admin or the customer's CSM per the API Keys doc, so credentials require being an enterprise customer.
REST endpoints under {baseUrl}/api/rest/v1/ with Bearer tokens.
Intapp's DealCloud API docs document the DealCloud MCP Server with OAuth 2.0 and .well-known discovery for Claude/ChatGPT/Copilot clients.
Buildable with a customer site's API key, but gated on being an enterprise customer with API capability enabled; the enum lists 'enterprise customer' as a caveat gate.
'The Pylon API uses Bearer authentication' with admin-created API tokens; no OAuth app option is documented for the REST API.
No free plan; plans are booked via demo/sales and 'Pylon offers free trials for prospects' set up by a sales rep, so credentials come only through sales.
Feature table lists 'REST API' and 'Webhooks' on Professional, Advanced and Enterprise.
Pylon docs document its hosted MCP server at https://mcp.usepylon.com (US) and https://mcp.eu.usepylon.com (EU).
Full REST API exists but testing requires a sales-provisioned trial or paid customer account.

'You need to create an OAuth2 application before you can use the API'; the Authorization Code flow 'is typically used for integrations to be used by other Help Scout users', with no review step described.

'The Free plan does not include access to the API or integrations'; API is on Standard/Plus/Pro, and the pricing FAQ gives a 15-day no-card trial of Standard/Plus with all plan features, so the free path to credentials is trial-only.
Inbox (Mailbox) API 2.0 is a REST API with per-plan rate limits (200/400/800 calls per minute).
Help Scout docs: 'Help Scout MCP gives AI assistants secure, official access', endpoint https://mcp.helpscout.net/mcp, on Standard/Plus/Pro.
Buildable via self-serve OAuth app, but API needs a paid tier after the 15-day trial (Free plan excluded).
API keys are for private apps only; OAuth2 is mandatory for public apps installed by other merchants.

Public apps must be submitted on the Developer Portal for Gorgias review (with a test account) before they are listed/installable; sandbox is a trial account converted by the partnerships team. Review outranks the trial gate under v2 precedence.
Gorgias exposes a REST API (tickets, customers, macros, etc.) authenticated by API key or OAuth2 bearer token.
Gorgias announces 'a first-party server' in open beta, included at no extra cost on any plan.
Buildable and testable via trial/sandbox, but public multi-tenant launch needs Gorgias app review.
'Each bot is given a unique authentication token' from BotFather, passed in the URL path https://api.telegram.org/bot<token>/METHOD_NAME (a static key, not OAuth).
Anyone can create a bot via BotFather and get a token at no cost; no review or install cap is documented.
HTTP-based API over HTTPS supporting GET/POST with query, form or JSON parameters (RPC-style HTTP; rest is the closest enum value).
Telegram's Bot API docs make no mention of MCP, and searching turned up only community servers (sparfenyuk, chigwell, overpod, lexfrei), none on Telegram's domains.
Free, instant bot tokens and a documented HTTP API mean a toolkit can be built and tested today.
Get-started page: API authentication uses Threads user access tokens that conform to the OAuth 2.0 protocol.
Users without a role on the app can grant permissions only after each permission passes App Review and the app is published, so multi-tenant use needs Meta review.
Endpoints are plain HTTP GET/POST Graph-style resources (e.g. GET /refresh_access_token); no GraphQL or SOAP.
Meta's MCP hub lists only Meta Ads, Meta Social Technologies (devtools) and WhatsApp Business Tools servers, none for Threads; Threads MCPs found are third-party.
Buildable and testable with tester accounts today, but App Review gates launch to other users.

Creating an application under Settings > Advanced yields an Application ID/Secret for the OAuth2 flow (third-party doc; gumroad.com/api is client-rendered and returned no text); Gumroad's own MCP also uses OAuth.
Gumroad has no monthly fee (free to join, per-sale fee only) and any account can create an API application; no review or install cap found.
UNSETTLED: the official API page is client-rendered and returned no text to fetch, so REST could not be confirmed from an opened page; no evidence of another style.
Gumroad, Inc. documents its own remote MCP endpoint https://gumroad.com/claude/v1/mcp with OAuth access to the user's store.
Self-serve OAuth credentials at $0 and an official MCP; nothing blocks building and testing today.
API authenticates with an API token created in Console, sent as Bearer; the API docs do not mention OAuth (OAuth exists only for the MCP server).
Free plan at $0 with $5 monthly usage, no credit card, renews monthly (not a trial).
Docs: the API is organized around RESTful HTTP endpoints.
Apify hosts https://mcp.apify.com and publishes github.com/apify/apify-mcp-server.
Free self-serve token, REST API and an official MCP; no gate.
Public API requests authenticate with a Clay API key in the clay-api-key header; OAuth appears only for the MCP server.

API/CLI limits table includes a Free plan (100 results per 30 days) separate from Trial; pricing lists 'Build with Clay via CLI / API' on Free. Tables are Enterprise-only, which is a caveat rather than the access gate.
Public API is HTTP endpoints with request/response schemas; the CLI is secondary, so primary style is rest.
Clay runs the MCP server at https://api.clay.com/v3/mcp with OAuth+PKCE and open Dynamic Client Registration.
Buildable on Free, but tiny free result quotas, webhooks/HTTP API on Growth+ and Tables on Enterprise limit testing.
Query API supports Basic and Bearer auth; requests use a valid database user's login credentials, so basic (username/password) is the typical toolkit path.
AuraDB Free at $0, no credit card or payment method required; no app review for multi-tenant use since each user brings their own instance.
Query API is HTTP (POST /db/neo4j/query/v2); Bolt is driver-only, so for a toolkit the HTTP API is the primary style.
Repo in the neo4j GitHub org described as 'Neo4j official MCP Server', documented at neo4j.com/docs/mcp (local, username/password).
Free self-serve, but every tenant must supply its own instance URI and credentials (per-tenant setup caveat).
Docs: 'Any integrations that allow other users to grant access to Airtable should use OAuth.'
Free plan includes 1,000 API calls per workspace per month; the OAuth integration guide requires only privacy policy and terms URLs before sharing, with no review or install cap.
Docs: the API 'closely follows REST semantics.'
Airtable documents its own MCP server at https://mcp.airtable.com/mcp (OAuth or PAT), 'available to all users on all plans.'
Self-serve OAuth integration with no review step; free tier is enough to build and test (1,000 calls/month is a usage limit, not a gate).
Every request needs a dashboard-generated key (ipx_live_...) sent as Bearer in the Authorization header; OAuth is only listed as 'Coming Q3 2026' for QuickBooks/Stripe apps.

UNSETTLED: the developer page lists API tiers starting at a $99/mo Developer plan and the homepage says API access needs the Credit Pack or Unlimited plan, but the MCP server docs (ipayx.ai/docs/mcp-server) describe free tools at 10 audits/day per API key, so vendor pages conflict on a free key path.
Reference page is titled 'REST API · v1' (base URL is a Supabase edge function).
Vendor developer page documents its own MCP endpoint https://mcp.ipayx.ai/mcp (author iPayX Protocol), also documented at ipayx.ai/docs/mcp-server.
REST API and official MCP exist, but full API use sits behind paid tiers (free tier is 3 audits), so a paid gate limits testing.
